collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The council apologizes for an old wrong, and the family says words are not enough: make real repair, or let it stand.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Years ago, the elders' council took away (friend)'s family's fishing rights over a dispute that turned out to be someone else's fault. Today, (subject) apologized for the council in front of the whole village. (friend) listened, and said: thank you, and what about the fishing rights? What should the council do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The council restores the fishing rights and gives the family a new canoe. (friend) accepts. (friend.He/she) does not say the past is forgotten. (friend.He/she) says it is a start.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The council says the apology is all it can give. (friend) is not satisfied, and says so, plainly, at every gathering. The village begins to think (friend.he/she) has a point. The matter is not closed.
